finding.description: The per-picture slice counter is an unbounded int, while decoded macroblock ownership is stored in a uint16_t slice table initialized to 0xFFFF. On slice 65535, storing slice_num aliases the unused-entry sentinel. The picture initializer deliberately re-poisons the table's spare mb_stride column with that sentinel, so neighbor checks can treat padded entries as members of the current slice. With deblocking_filter == 2 at mb_x == 0, the false top-left match selects top_borders[top_idx][-1], one 96-byte macroblock record before the heap allocation, and the luma and chroma XCHG operations write through it. Later FFmpeg repair 6d57428858 rejects current_slice >= 0xFFFE before incrementing, independently confirming the exact collision boundary.
finding.code_snippet: sl->slice_num = ++h->current_slice;
finding.poc: Decode one H.264 picture containing at least 65535 accepted slices so slice_num becomes 0xFFFF, then reach a left-edge macroblock with deblocking_filter == 2 and a padded top-left slice-table entry; the sentinel collision enables the top_borders[-1] luma/chroma exchanges.

vulnerability_trace.summary: attacker-controlled slice count reaches a wider counter, truncates into the 16-bit ownership table as its 0xFFFF sentinel, and corrupts a neighbor-existence decision before luma and chroma exchanges through a pointer one 96-byte record before top_borders

steps.note: The 16-bit table uses 0xFFFF for unavailable/padded entries.
The active table has leading guard rows and an mb_stride equal to mb_width + 1, leaving a spare padding column.
Every frame re-poisons the active table, including the spare per-row column, with the colliding 0xFFFF sentinel.
No terminating bound prevents slice_num from reaching 65535.
The int counter is stored into the uint16_t table.
Six FMO/non-FMO comparisons use slice-table equality to decide whether top-left, top, left, and top-right neighbors exist; the collision reverses the intended unavailable-entry result.
Only the deblocking_filter == 2 branch consults the colliding entry; the alternative explicitly requires mb_x > 0.
At mb_x == 0 this forms a pointer one 96-byte top-border record before the allocation.
The falsely enabled luma exchange writes through the underflowed heap pointer; the 4:4:4 and non-4:4:4 chroma exchanges repeat the write at lines 573-574 and 586-587.

finding.description: The Vulkan HEVC start-frame path copies each current short- or long-term RPS list into a Vulkan StdVideoDecodeH265PictureInfo array whose API-defined capacity is 8. FFmpeg's parser and RPS builder allow an individual list to contain up to 15 short-term references or up to 16 retained references. Unlike the NVDEC path, the Vulkan path does not reject a list count above the destination capacity, so i >= 8 writes beyond RefPicSetStCurrBefore, RefPicSetStCurrAfter, or RefPicSetLtCurr into adjacent picture-info fields.

finding.poc: Use Vulkan HEVC decoding on a valid stream whose current short-term-before, short-term-after, or long-term RPS contains more than eight used references that resolve in the DPB.

vulnerability_trace.summary: bitstream RPS counts survive parser checks and RPS construction with more than eight members, then directly bound writes into three eight-entry Vulkan API arrays

finding.description: ff_rdt_parse_header skips leading RDT status packets while at least five bytes remain. It reads a packet-controlled 16-bit pkt_len and rejects only values greater than the remaining input. A zero length therefore passes validation, after which both buf and len are advanced by zero and the status-packet condition remains unchanged forever. A direct 16-byte header with the followed-by-data flag, status marker, and zero packet length deterministically consumes CPU until externally terminated.
finding.code_snippet: while (len >= 5 && buf[1] == 0xFF) { pkt_len = AV_RB16(buf + 3); if (pkt_len > len) return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA; buf += pkt_len; len -= pkt_len; }

finding.description: The RDT AAC cache path copies every unconsumed byte of a received record into a fixed RTP_MAX_PACKET_LENGTH plus padding buffer without checking the remaining length. An AAC VBR packet declaring one cached subpacket consumes only its four-byte count and length table, then returns a positive cache count. A 9216-byte record therefore makes production rdt_parse_packet copy 9212 bytes into the 8256-byte payload buffer. The direct production-parser harness deterministically aborts under ASan on a heap-buffer-overflow write in that memcpy on both sealed snapshots.

Repeating the parser-valid value across 24 maximum-order MMR pieces also exceeds the generator's constant 177-byte-per-piece allocation estimate, after which the always-on flush assertion aborts. A public libavfilter graph with a two-pixel-wide output, missing primary metadata, and present secondary metadata produces an ASan heap-buffer-overflow write in draw_dot on the third frame on both sealed snapshots.

finding.description: The shared DNN output-name parser allocates MAX_SUPPORTED_OUTPUTS_NB, exactly four, pointer slots and writes every parsed token into that array without reserving a terminator slot or enforcing the maximum. It then unconditionally stores a NULL terminator at parsed_vals[val_num]. TensorFlow detection explicitly requires four output names, so its intended count writes the terminator into a fifth pointer slot. A production ff_dnn_init harness with four generic output names produces an ASan heap-buffer-overflow before backend lookup or model loading on both snapshots.
finding.code_snippet: parsed_vals = av_calloc(MAX_SUPPORTED_OUTPUTS_NB, sizeof(*parsed_vals)); ... parsed_vals[val_num++] = val; ... parsed_vals[val_num] = NULL;

finding.description: TensorFlow inference allocates and returns task->nb_output tensors, and the registered TensorFlow detection path requires four outputs. Cleanup attempts to derive that runtime count with sizeof(*output_tensors) divided by sizeof(output_tensors[0]); both operands describe one pointer, so the result is always one. Only the first TensorFlow output tensor is deleted before the pointer array is freed. Every processed detection frame therefore leaks three complete model output tensors, allowing sustained valid use to exhaust memory. The sealed builds omit TensorFlow, so this remains source-confirmed rather than dynamically reproduced.
finding.code_snippet: int nb_output = sizeof(*request->output_tensors)/sizeof(request->output_tensors[0]); for (i = 0; i < nb_output; ++i) TF_DeleteTensor(...);
finding.poc: Configure vf_dnn_detect with its required four-output TensorFlow model and process frames while monitoring output-tensor allocations; three of four tensors per request are not passed to TF_DeleteTensor.

vulnerability_trace.summary: four TensorFlow outputs are produced per detection frame, but pointer-type sizeof arithmetic hard-codes cleanup to one tensor

Both sizeof operands are one pointer, making nb_output equal one regardless of the task.

finding.description: The NellyMoser encoder's optional trellis search caps idx_max with OPT_SIZE but rejects a candidate only when idx is greater than that inclusive cap. An exactly-OPT_SIZE transition therefore indexes one element beyond a trellis row. Those transitions are reachable from ordinary audio samples, and repeated row-edge writes can corrupt the following row; at the final band the corresponding read crosses the end of the complete allocation. A short public white-noise encode with volume 10 and trellis enabled produces UBSan reports for opt and path at index 35768 followed by an ASan heap-buffer-overflow read exactly after the 3,290,656-byte opt allocation on both sealed snapshots.
finding.code_snippet: idx_max = FFMIN(OPT_SIZE, cand[band - 1] + q); ... if (idx > idx_max) break; ... opt[band][idx]
finding.poc: Run evaluations/run_ffmpeg_nellymoser_trellis_reproducer.py against either sealed sanitizer-instrumented FFmpeg binary.

vulnerability_trace.summary: an inclusive upper bound admits trellis state OPT_SIZE even though every row's final legal state is OPT_SIZE minus one

Equality is accepted, so the invalid one-past state reaches both trellis arrays.

A public libavcodec harness decodes and unreferences a raw 16x16 gray frame, then supplies a 300-byte frame with a valid table and a two-byte compressed slice containing no samples. FFmpeg returns a second frame whose 256 bytes are a reversible transformation of the entire prior pooled frame on both sealed snapshots.

finding.description: The RTP/AV1 depacketizer intentionally discards temporal-delimiter and tile-list OBUs, but that branch advances the output packet cursor and remaining input length without advancing the input cursor. The next loop iteration therefore parses bytes inside the ignored OBU as a new element while retaining an output cursor displaced by the complete ignored size. Packet growth accounts only for the newly parsed element, so its header or payload write begins beyond the allocated packet. A direct production-handler harness with a 100-byte temporal delimiter followed by 17 bytes produces an ASan heap-buffer-overflow write 19 bytes beyond an 81-byte allocation on both sealed snapshots.
finding.code_snippet: if (obu_type == AV1_OBU_TEMPORAL_DELIMITER || obu_type == AV1_OBU_TILE_LIST) { pktpos += obu_size; rem_pkt_size -= obu_size; ... continue; }

vulnerability_trace.summary: discarding an ignored OBU advances only the logical output cursor and remaining length, so a following parser iteration grows a small packet and writes through a large unallocated gap

steps.note: An RTP-controlled LEB declares the size of a temporal-delimiter or tile-list OBU.
These two OBU types enter the discard path.
The branch moves the output cursor and consumes the declared remaining length but never performs buf_ptr += obu_size.
The next iteration grows storage only for the bytes parsed from inside the ignored OBU, not for the gap already added to pktpos.
ASan observes the resulting write beyond the heap packet allocation before payload copying.

finding.description: Whisper allocates its audio queue from the queue duration, whose public minimum is 20 ms or 320 samples. It consumes complete upstream AVFrames without imposing a sample maximum. When one frame contains more samples than the queue, the capacity guard first transcribes at most the existing fill, then unconditionally copies the entire oversized frame into the fixed queue. FFmpeg's public asetnsamples filter can produce frames up to INT_MAX samples, establishing that no framework contract restricts an audio frame to the Whisper queue capacity. The sealed builds omit the optional Whisper dependency, so this remains source-confirmed rather than dynamically reproduced.
finding.code_snippet: if (fill + samples > queue_size) run_transcription(ctx, frame, fill); memcpy(audio_buffer + fill, input_data, samples * sizeof(*audio_buffer));

vulnerability_trace.summary: the filter's duration-sized queue can be smaller than one valid upstream audio frame, but its overflow guard drains only prior contents before copying that whole frame

finding.description: RTP/LATM encodes an AAC access unit's size as one length byte per 255 payload bytes, but never ensures that this variable-length header fits the fixed RTP packet buffer before writing it. The public RTP muxer accepts AVPackets independently of the output packet size. With a normal 1,472-byte packet sink, a 382,500-byte AAC packet creates a 1,501-byte header; memset writes 1,500 bytes into the 1,472-byte allocation and ASan reports a heap-buffer-overflow on both sealed snapshots. The following fragmentation arithmetic would also become negative once the header exceeds max_payload_size.
finding.code_snippet: header_size = size/0xFF + 1; memset(s->buf, 0xFF, header_size - 1);

finding.description: The RTP muxer accepts every packet sink larger than its 12-byte common header, but codec packetizers reserve additional payload headers without checking their own minimum. A public muxer configured with a valid 13-byte packet sink therefore has one payload byte. H.263 RFC2190 derives a fragment length of -7 and RFC4629 derives -1; their resynchronization paths preserve those values before memcpy. H.261 independently subtracts its four-byte header, preserves -3 through its reverse marker search, and reaches memcpy through the public muxer. ASan reports negative-size-param for all three variants of the same undersized-RTP-payload root.

finding.description: FFV1 level-4 remapping allocates each decoded lookup table for exactly slice_width times slice_height entries and records the number of populated entries, but entropy symbols are decoded in a ceil(log2(remap_count))-bit space. For a non-power-of-two remap count, the mask therefore admits unused indices; when pixel_num is below that power-of-two ceiling, those indices are also outside the physical table. A valid 513x1 yuv444p16le remapped FFV1 packet has this shape. Flipping one entropy bit at packet byte 18 makes decode_line produce an out-of-range masked symbol, and decode_plane performs a two-byte heap-buffer-overflow read on both sealed snapshots.
finding.code_snippet: ((uint16_t*)(src + stride*y))[x*pixel_stride] = sc->fltmap[remap_index][sample[1][x] & mask];

vulnerability_trace.summary: a bitstream-defined non-power-of-two remap count is represented by a wider power-of-two symbol alphabet, and an unused entropy symbol indexes beyond the pixel-count-sized lookup table

The entropy alphabet and mask round that count up to the next power of two without constraining unused symbols.
Packet-controlled entropy data can produce any symbol in the rounded bit-width; the reproducer's single-bit mutation reaches an unused one.
The unused symbol is used directly as a lookup index; ASan reports a two-byte heap-buffer-overflow read in decode_plane on both snapshots.

A public 1x200 bitmap subtitle and a 142-byte caller buffer pass the 100-byte RLE budget check but require 200 RLE bytes; ASan reports a stack-buffer-overflow in dvd_encode_rle on both sealed snapshots.

finding.description: The common D3D12VA decoder allocates its fixed upload resource from the decoded frame's raw-image buffer size, but the H.264, HEVC, VC-1, VP9, and AV1 backends copy accepted compressed frame data into that mapped resource without checking the resulting byte count. Compressed-picture size is not bounded by decoded-image size. H.264 and HEVC additionally prepend three bytes per slice, VC-1 can prepend four-byte start codes, and AV1 can first accumulate partial tile groups into a separate heap buffer with the same raw-image-sized capacity before copying the unbounded total into the resource. The durable proof generates a standards-valid, normally decodable 16x5400 yuv420p H.264 Baseline stream whose slice bytes plus inserted prefixes exceed both the resource's 129,600-byte declared width and its 131,072-byte 64 KiB-aligned allocation floor. A valid 16x16 HEVC Main stream independently exceeds its 384-byte declared resource width. Later FFmpeg repairs add the missing capacity checks to the VC-1, VP9, and AV1 mapped copies and to AV1 accumulation, independently confirming those variants. The exact H.264 and HEVC byte counts are deterministically recorded by the proof script and can vary slightly with the installed encoder build. No Windows D3D12 runtime was available, so the root is retained as source-, producer-, and repair-confirmed rather than sanitizer-observed.

finding.description: Libxavs advertises encoder delay, so a public flush before any input frame reaches XAVS_frame with a null frame and a zero-initialized out_frame_count. The direct production-function proof uses max_b_frames=2 and a valid zero-NAL library result; ASan reports an eight-byte heap read immediately before the three-entry ring.

finding.description: The production WMS SDP parser base64-decodes a server-controlled RTSP-MS/ASF header and passes it to rtp_asf_fix_header. If that object's GUID differs from the file-header GUID and its 64-bit size is zero, the vulnerable branch's sole upper-bound check accepts it and advances the loop pointer by zero. The do/while condition remains true forever, consuming one RTSP demuxing thread. A differential production-function proof times out on the pinned build, while exact repair 11d5f475be rejects the same payload and returns immediately; the repair explicitly identifies the infinite loop.
finding.code_snippet: if (memcmp(p, ff_asf_file_header, sizeof(ff_asf_guid))) { if (chunksize > end - p) return -1; p += chunksize; continue; }

finding.description: The public Icecast output protocol accepts stream metadata through string AVOptions and concatenates each nonempty value directly into its custom HTTP-header block. A value such as `safe-name\r\nX-Injected: yes` therefore terminates `Ice-Name` and creates a second attacker-chosen outbound header when the HTTP protocol appends that block verbatim. A loopback public `avio_open2` proof captures both headers from the pinned build. The identical proof against exact repair 99e1ecca36 captures neither header and logs its new CR/LF rejection. Scope requires an application to place untrusted data in an Icecast metadata option; ordinary media payload bytes do not control the value.
finding.code_snippet: if (NOT_EMPTY(value)) av_bprintf(bp, "%s: %s\r\n", key, value); ... av_dict_set(&opt_dict, "headers", headers, AV_DICT_DONT_STRDUP_VAL);

vulnerability_trace.summary: an untrusted Icecast metadata value crosses a CRLF boundary into a verbatim outbound HTTP-header block

The exact later repair rejects metadata header values containing CR or LF and credits a security report.

finding.description: The public AV1 dovi_rpu bitstream filter assumes every successfully parsed Dolby Vision RPU produces replacement metadata. The parser deliberately returns success for an unrecognized RPU type, after which ff_dovi_get_metadata reports no metadata and update_rpu returns a NULL pointer with size zero. The AV1 path wraps that result in an AVBufferRef, changes the payload pointer to address 1, and assigns -1 to its unsigned payload size. CBS serialization then reads from address 1 while iterating the effectively unbounded payload. A public 56-byte AV1 metadata OBU deterministically aborts under ASan in cbs_av1_write_obu on the pinned build; exact repair 534f16d866 adds the missing no-RPU guard, and the identical packet is emitted cleanly.
finding.code_snippet: ref = av_buffer_create(rpu, rpu_size, av_buffer_default_free, NULL, 0); ... t35->payload = rpu + 1; t35->payload_size = rpu_size - 1;

vulnerability_trace.summary: a valid AV1 Dolby metadata unit whose RPU parser returns success without metadata becomes a NULL/zero replacement, then pointer and size underflow make CBS serialize from address one

steps.note: The crafted public packet is a size-delimited AV1 ITU-T T.35 metadata OBU with the US country code and a sufficient payload.
Packet bytes select Dolby provider 0x003B and provider-oriented code 0x00000800, entering the RPU rewrite path.
The inner EMDF payload supplies RPU type zero, for which parsing intentionally succeeds without populating metadata.
The no-metadata state is explicitly represented to the caller as a successful NULL pointer and zero size.
The vulnerable caller accepts the NULL/zero result and creates a zero-sized buffer reference around it.
NULL plus one becomes address 1, while zero minus one becomes SIZE_MAX in the size_t payload field.
The CBS writer immediately reads from address 1; ASan reports the SEGV through cbs_av1_write_obu.
The exact later repair checks the missing postcondition before constructing the AV1 payload and identifies the issue as an out-of-array access.

finding.description: MVC2 stores its 128-entry RGB palette in an uninitialized stack array, initializes only the packet-declared number of colors, and later accepts seven-bit palette indices without checking them against that count. Compiling the vulnerable decoder source under deterministic pattern and zero automatic-variable initialization produces `pixel=aaaaaaaa` and `pixel=00000000` respectively through the identical public avcodec packet path, proving that stack contents cross into the decoded frame. A repair must reject every index greater than or equal to `nb_colors`; zero-initializing the array is only the differential proof.

finding.description: VBLE forces YUV420P output and sizes its symbol buffer with FFmpeg's complete image-geometry helper, but it decodes both chroma planes with `width / 2` and `height / 2`. YUV420P instead uses ceiling subsampling for odd dimensions. A public 3x3 decoder proof supplies seventeen valid zero-length symbols and a `get_buffer2` callback that fills the codec-owned frame with 0xA5. The luma plane and first sample in each logical 2x2 chroma plane are decoded to zero, while the other six visible U/V samples remain 0xA5: `u=00a5/a5a5 v=00a5/a5a5`. The decoder therefore publishes prior buffer contents as visible chroma on odd-width or odd-height frames.

finding.description: The S/PDIF probe checks for a seven-byte AAC ADTS header as though parsing started at the four-byte sync boundary, but spdif_get_offset_and_codec actually receives &buf[5]. The durable production-source proof passes a 14-byte logical buffer in a 15-byte allocation whose tail byte completes an ADTS header: the pinned probe sets codec=AAC, while exact repair 15bbf3a21d adds the missing byte to the bound and leaves the codec unset. The repair explicitly identifies an OSS-Fuzz read of uninitialized memory.

finding.description: The D3D12 MPEG-2 accelerator allocates each upload resource at a fixed size derived from the decoded software-frame geometry, independently accumulates the compressed sizes of as many as 1,024 attacker-controlled slices, and copies that complete compressed bitstream into the mapped upload resource without comparing the two sizes. A sufficiently large validly framed MPEG-2 picture therefore writes past the GPU upload buffer from the CPU. Exact repair 26a9f9b3ae adds the missing ctx_pic->bitstream_size > ctx->bitstream_size guard immediately before mapping and copying. This remains source-confirmed because the current host has neither Windows nor a D3D12 decode device.

finding.description: The PowerPC AltiVec vertical YUV-to-packed-RGB scaler is installed for RGB24/BGR24 and four 32-bit RGB layouts without requiring the destination width to be a multiple of sixteen. Its loop runs while i < dstW but every iteration emits a complete sixteen-pixel vector: 48 bytes for 24-bit output or 64 bytes for 32-bit output. The final iteration therefore writes past an exact-size destination row whenever dstW is not a multiple of sixteen. The apparent tail handler cannot contain the write because the loop exits with i >= dstW and its condition is `if (i < dstW)`. The public sws_scale API accepts caller-owned exact-size output buffers, so even a one-pixel destination can receive the full vector store. This remains source-confirmed because the current arm64 host cannot execute AltiVec code.
finding.code_snippet: for (i = 0; i < dstW; i += 16) { ... out_rgba(R, G, B, out); } if (i < dstW) { i -= 16; ... }
finding.poc: On a PowerPC host with AltiVec enabled but without a replacing VSX general-X implementation, use public sws_scale with a non-multiple-of-16 destination width, a general vertical filter, one of the installed RGB24/BGR24/ABGR/BGRA/ARGB/RGBA outputs, and an exact-size destination allocation; ASan should report the final 48- or 64-byte vector store beyond the row.

vulnerability_trace.summary: an unguarded non-multiple-of-sixteen destination reaches an AltiVec loop whose final iteration writes a complete packed-RGB vector beyond the public output buffer

steps.note: The normal AltiVec dispatch checks flags, alpha, and output format but imposes no destination-width alignment requirement.
The same assignment is made for six packed RGB layouts, making the vector routine the general vertical scaler.
The general public scaling path forwards the caller's output row and exact destination width unchanged.
Any positive remainder starts one final iteration even though fewer than sixteen output pixels remain.
The selected macro performs three 16-byte stores for 24-bit output or four for 32-bit output, overrunning an exact-size partial row.
After the loop, i is always greater than or equal to dstW, so the scratch-based partial handler is dead and cannot prevent the vector overrun.

finding.description: The OpenColorIO filter accepts a public output pixel-format option and allocates its output AVFrame in that selected format, but query_formats() gives every input and output link the same common format list and never advertises the selected output separately. A larger RIST payload therefore overruns the caller-owned FIFO destination. Exact later repair 8880a174d0 clamps payload_len to the supplied size and explicitly identifies out-of-array access. The local sanitizer build lacks librist and network support, so this root remains source-confirmed rather than dynamically reproduced.
finding.code_snippet: size = data_block->payload_len; memcpy(buf, data_block->payload, size);
finding.poc: Open async:rist://... so async's background ring requests 4096 bytes, then deliver a valid RIST payload larger than 4096 bytes. The vulnerable protocol copies the full payload into that smaller FIFO span; exact repair 8880a174d0 changes the assignment to FFMIN(data_block->payload_len, size).

vulnerability_trace.summary: the RIST URL protocol discards its caller's capacity and copies a larger received payload into the smaller destination

steps.note: The async wrapper exposes a concrete production caller that reserves and requests at most 4,096 bytes.

RIST payloads through 9,972 bytes are accepted, which can exceed async's 4,096-byte destination.
The caller-provided capacity is discarded and replaced with attacker-controlled received length.

finding.description: MCC compressed aliases X and Y map to keys 33 and 34 with length zero and value NULL. A public time-code line containing either alias reaches bytestream2_put_buffer, which unconditionally passes that NULL source to memcpy even though the selected length is zero. Passing a null pointer to the library copy operation violates its pointer precondition. Exact later repair e27d91ca71 skips bytestream2_put_buffer whenever the alias length is zero and explicitly identifies passing a NULL pointer. Apple Clang optimizes the zero-byte copy away without a sanitizer diagnostic, so this root is source-confirmed rather than counted as dynamically reproduced.
finding.code_snippet: { .key = 33, .len = 0, .value = NULL }; ... bytestream2_put_buffer(&pb, aliases[idx].value, aliases[idx].len);

finding.description: The OpenSSL TLS backend enables certificate-chain verification for verify=1 but installs a peer-identity target only when the URL host is nonnumeric. A numeric-IP client therefore verifies that the server certificate chains to a trusted CA without requiring an iPAddress SAN matching the requested address, so any trusted certificate for any name is accepted. A local CA signs a certificate only for wrong.example and with no IP SAN; OpenSSL independently accepts its chain and rejects it for 127.0.0.1, while FFmpeg's public tls://127.0.0.1 URL with verify=1 completes the connection. Exact later repair 83c6922826 binds numeric hosts through X509_VERIFY_PARAM_set1_ip and explicitly identifies acceptance of any publicly trusted certificate for any name.

finding.description: The Vulkan horizontal, vertical, and combined flip shaders calculate mirrored zero-based coordinates as dimension minus position instead of dimension minus one minus position. The dispatch guard admits every valid output coordinate, so output x=0 makes horizontal flip load input x=width, output y=0 makes vertical flip load y=height, and combined flip crosses one or both bounds along its first row and column. The exact source-and-geometry proof exhausts a 4x3 frame and finds three, four, and six invalid image loads respectively. Later compile-time shader refactor d0ee5d0556 moves the same coordinate to the destination store without adding the missing subtraction, and current origin/master still contains the out-of-range transform. No Vulkan runtime was available locally.
finding.code_snippet: imageLoad(input_image[i], ivec2(size.x - pos.x, pos.y)); ... imageLoad(input_image[i], ivec2(pos.x, size.y - pos.y));
finding.poc: Run evaluations/run_ffmpeg_flip_vulkan_coordinate_proof.py against the pinned checkout. Its ignored report validates the exact shader expressions and exhaustively records every out-of-range coordinate for a 4x3 public frame with expected_observed=true.

vulnerability_trace.summary: each Vulkan flip mode mirrors zero-based image coordinates around dimension rather than dimension minus one, crossing the image boundary on the first output row or column

steps.note: The guard dispatches all ordinary zero-based output positions from (0,0) through (width-1,height-1).
At every first-column invocation x=0, horizontal flip derives x=width, one texel beyond the input image.
At every first-row invocation y=0, vertical flip derives y=height, one texel beyond the input image.
Combined flip crosses the x or y boundary for the union of the first column and first row.
The public Vulkan filter runs the generated shader on matching negotiated input and output frame geometry; mismatched images are not required to reach the invalid coordinates.

finding.description: The Nellymoser decoder derives a signed-int block count from the public packet size, then multiplies it by 256 in signed int to allocate the output frame while retaining the original block count for decoding. A 1,073,741,888-byte packet contains 16,777,217 complete blocks and makes the product wrap from 4,294,967,552 to 256 samples. FFmpeg consequently allocates one 1,024-byte float block, then the second production decode iteration writes exactly beyond that allocation. A valid demand-zero virtual mapping backs the complete packet; UBSan records the signed count overflow and ASan records the heap overflow. Exact later repair 2864ce5e28 rejects block counts above INT_MAX / NELLY_SAMPLES and identifies an out-of-array access.

Its ignored report records the valid 1,073,741,888-byte mapped packet, signed overflow, exact 1,024-byte output allocation, second-block production write, exact repair, and expected_observed=true.

vulnerability_trace.summary: Nellymoser's signed 256-times-block-count expression wraps to one output block while its decode loop remains proportional to all 16,777,217 packet blocks

The exact proof size is divisible by 64 and yields 16,777,217 complete blocks.
The vulnerable tree rejects only non-positive counts, so the large positive count proceeds.

The wrapped count allocates exactly 256 float samples, a 1,024-byte output region.
The production loop keeps the original 16,777,217-block count rather than the wrapped frame count.

finding.description: The VC2 encoder stores intermediate wavelet coefficients in signed 32-bit dwtcoef arrays and repeatedly feeds the low-low subdivision through up to five transform levels. The 9/7 lifting stages multiply and add those attacker-controlled coefficients in signed int, so sufficiently amplified values overflow before the right shift. Public OSS-Fuzz testcase 5310290362433536 reaches this path through the VC2 encoder and was reported as an integer overflow in vc2_subband_dwt_97. Exact later repair 5f91556215 changes the working representation to uint32_t and explicitly casts each lifting sum back to dwtcoef before its arithmetic shift, preserving intended wrap semantics without signed undefined behavior. Follow-up repair 7c7ca349bc applies the same correction to the 5/3 and Haar variants. The public testcase did not reproduce under the local Darwin sanitizer build, so this consolidated transform-family root remains source-confirmed rather than counted as a local dynamic reproduction.

Each low-low result is fed into the next transform level, amplifying intermediate coefficients.

finding.description: The RTP/DV depacketizer starts a dynamic buffer for a frame and appends every accepted payload fragment. It releases an incomplete frame only when the attacker-controlled RTP timestamp changes and publishes it only when a marker bit arrives. An in-sequence sender can therefore keep one timestamp and omit every marker indefinitely; no known fixed DV frame-size limit is enforced, so the receiver withholds output while retaining all payload bytes up to the generic dynamic buffer's INT_MAX ceiling. A production-handler proof sends 4,096 valid 2,048-byte non-marker fragments with one timestamp and observes all 8,388,608 bytes retained with zero output packets. RTP sequence validation explicitly supports 16-bit wraps, so it does not impose a frame-fragment cap. No post-pin change on the selected path adds a bound.
finding.code_snippet: avio_write(rtp_dv_ctx->buf, buf, len); if (!(flags & RTP_FLAG_MARKER)) return AVERROR(EAGAIN);
finding.poc: Run evaluations/run_ffmpeg_rtp_dv_unbounded_buffer_reproducer.py against the configured pinned tree. Its ignored report records 4,096 same-timestamp, non-marker fragments, exact eight-MiB retention, zero output packets, the generic INT_MAX ceiling, and expected_observed=true.

vulnerability_trace.summary: a remote RTP sender can suppress both timestamp changes and marker bits while every DV fragment accumulates in one dynamic buffer toward a two-gigabyte ceiling

finding.description: The Linux fbdev output exposes xoffset and yoffset across the complete signed-int domain but performs its offscreen clipping arithmetic before constraining those values. With any positive video width and xoffset=INT_MAX, video_width+xoffset overflows before the guard can reject the frame; xoffset or yoffset equal to INT_MIN independently overflows the unary-negation checks. The committed portable proof executes the exact horizontal expression and UBSan aborts. In ordinary wrapped execution the bad values can survive into signed size arithmetic and mapped-framebuffer pointer adjustments before memcpy. Full muxer execution is Linux-device-gated, so this is retained as a low-severity public-configuration denial of service rather than an arbitrary-write claim. No later repair is present on current origin/master.
